newsitem.title: UK: Rain breaks dry spell in south-east England.
newsitem.headline: Rain breaks dry spell in south-east England.

text.p: Up to 18 mm of rain fell on London and south-eastern Britain during a three-day period from Friday to Sunday, the London Weather Centre said on Sunday.
"Most of Northern Ireland, England and Wales had a good bit of rain but Scotland got off lightly," a spokesman for the centre told Reuters.
More rain was also predicted throughout most parts of the country on Monday with a forecast of occasional showers and then dryer weather later in the week, he added.

A dry spell in much of northwest Europe has helped drive world wheat prices to 1997 highs around $4.25 per bushel in Chicago futures. The European Union imposed a tax on Thursday to curb wheat exports and thereby keep a lid on internal prices.

Although heavy rain fell throughout most of the weekend it was the only significant rainfall since March 4, the centre spokesman said, adding that he doubted it would make much of an impact on the drought throughout most of the country.
"It was a good strong rain but it will take more than that to fill up the reservoirs," he said.
